title: Step 1: Hook - A Sinking Mystery
text: Ayesha is washing her hands. The soap slips and falls into the bucket of water. Oh no! It sinks. But wait, the plastic soap case she puts it in floats! How can the heavy soap case float while the soap sinks?

title: Step 2: Socratic Thinking
text: Have you ever noticed an iron nail sink in water, but a huge ship made of iron floats on the ocean? Why do you think this happens? Can you predict what will happen if we put an empty plastic bottle in water, and then fill it with water and put it in again?

content.title: Step 3: Discovery - Pushing Water Away
content.description: Notice how the empty bottle pushes water away to make room for itself, and the water pushes back up! This is why it floats.

title: Step 4: Reveal - Density and Buoyancy
text: When an object pushes away water equal to its own weight, it floats! This is why flat things or things with air inside them (like an empty bottle or a ship) float. The water pushes back up! This upward push is called Buoyancy.

content.definition: The upward push exerted by a liquid on an object placed in it.

question: What will happen to an empty, sealed plastic bottle when placed in water?
options: It will sink to the bottom

title: Step 6: Reflection
text: Next time you take a bath, try to push an empty mug upside down into a bucket of water. Do you feel the water pushing back up? That's buoyancy in action!

title: Step 7: Connection
text: This upward push of water is the same reason why you feel lighter when you swim in a pool. It is also the reason why hot air balloons float in the air, because air also pushes things up!

content.title: Step 8: Mastery - Foil Experiment
content.text: Take a bowl of water. Try floating a piece of aluminium foil. Now crumple it into a tight ball and drop it in. What happens? Write your observation!

title: Step 1: Hook - The Magic Sugar
text: Suguna is making tea. She adds sugar to the hot water and stirs. Suddenly, the sugar disappears! Where did it go? Did it vanish like magic?

title: Step 2: Socratic Thinking
text: If you mix sand in water, does it disappear too? Why does sugar 'vanish' but sand stays at the bottom? What is happening to the sugar?

content.title: Step 3: Discovery - Mixing with Water
content.description: Watch how the sugar molecules break apart into tiny invisible pieces and hide between the water molecules, while the heavy sand particles sink and clump at the bottom.

title: Step 4: Reveal - Soluble and Insoluble
text: When a substance mixes completely with water and we can't see it anymore, we say it has dissolved in water. These substances are called Soluble (like sugar and salt). If it does not mix and stays at the bottom, it is called Insoluble (like sand or chalk powder).

content.definition: A substance that can be completely dissolved in a liquid.

question: Which of the following substances will NOT dissolve in water?

content.title: Melting vs Dissolving
content.text: Students often think that 'melting' and 'dissolving' are the same thing. Melting is when a solid turns into a liquid because of heat (like ice melting). Dissolving is when a substance mixes completely into a liquid (like sugar in water).

title: Step 6: Reflection
text: If you want to make lemonade quickly, would you use cold water or normal water to dissolve the sugar? Think about how stirring or temperature affects dissolving!

title: Step 7: Connection
text: This property of water being able to dissolve so many things is why the sea is salty! Rivers dissolve salts from rocks and carry them to the ocean. Water is known as a 'Universal Solvent'.

content.title: Step 8: Mastery - The Kitchen Scientist
content.text: Gather 5 transparent glasses. Try to dissolve these items in water: salt, soil, turmeric powder, oil, and mustard seeds. Note down which ones are soluble, insoluble, or float on top!

title: Step 1: Hook - The Disappearing Puddle
text: It rained heavily in the morning, and there was a big puddle in front of your house. By evening, the sun came out and the puddle was completely dry! Where did the water go? Did someone drink it?

title: Step 2: Socratic Thinking
text: When we boil water in a pan, the water level goes down. If we leave wet clothes on a clothesline in the sun, they dry up. What do the sun and the stove have in common that makes the water disappear?

content.title: Step 3: Discovery - Heat and Water
content.description: See how heat gives energy to the water drops, making them move very fast and fly up into the air as invisible gas.

title: Step 4: Reveal - Evaporation
text: When water gets warm from the sun or a stove, it turns from a liquid into a gas called water vapor. This invisible gas floats up into the air. This process is called Evaporation. It's how clothes dry and how puddles disappear!

content.definition: The process of a liquid turning into a gas, usually due to heat.

question: What happens to water during evaporation?

content.title: Historical Connection
content.text: Remind students about the Dandi March where Gandhiji made salt. Sea water was collected in shallow pits. The sun evaporated the water, leaving the solid salt behind!

title: Step 6: Reflection
text: Why do we spread our clothes out to dry them, instead of keeping them folded? How does spreading them help evaporation happen faster?

title: Step 7: Connection
text: Evaporation is the very first step of the Water Cycle! The sun evaporates water from rivers and oceans. This water vapor goes up into the sky, forms clouds, and eventually comes back down as rain.

content.title: Step 8: Mastery - The Sunlight Race
content.text: Take two identical plates. Put 2 spoons of water in each. Keep one plate in direct sunlight and the other inside a dark room. Check after 2 hours. Which plate is dry? Why did it happen?
